Whenever Mint boots up the audio is stuffed until I fiddle with shit. I've got the audio going from the HDMI on the GPU (nVidia GTX680) to the monitor and from the monitor via aux out to the speakers (I have to do it this way because I'm using an HDMI dongle switch for the Wii U also attached to the monitor).

A couple of questions.

  1. How can I remove or disable the audio options and settings I don't want?

  2. How can I set the audio settings to load up the ones I want at default?

Here's are some pictures to show what I'm dealing with.

Hardware tab.

I only want the HDMI and the Logitech headset options there. But here's the annoying thing.

The HDMI audio option will only work if I have it set to a particular identical option, the fourth-one-down option in this drop down box.

More audio options I don't use. I only use the Logitech microphone. Not really an issue but I haven't start trying to play games online yet. Who knows what mic issues I'll run in to shortly.

The most straightforward way to change / disable Pulseaudio devices is to edit the config file in ~/.config/pulse. (Or /etc/pulse/default.pa if you want it to be system-wide.)

To disable a device, add set-card-profile alsa_card.pci-0000_01_00.1 off. (Use pactl list short cards to see the name of each card.)

To set the default sink, use set-default-sink <SINK NAME>, where <SINK NAME> is from pactl list short sinks. (Do the same for the microphone, but replace sink with source.)

The full documentation for this file is in man pulse-cli-syntax.
